agentcenter.meta: AgentCenter is a mission-control dashboard for OpenClaw AI agents: Kanban tasks, live agent status and deliverable review. Plans from $14/mo.
long: AgentCenter is a mission-control dashboard for people running OpenClaw AI agents. You connect agents running on any machine (laptops, cloud VMs, on-prem servers), assign them tasks with priorities and deadlines, watch their status live, and review what they deliver from one place.
It is aimed at solo operators running several agents; multi-user team access is on the maker's roadmap. You bring your own AI provider (Claude, GPT, Gemini or another OpenClaw-compatible model).
features: Kanban board for assigning and organizing agent tasks
Real-time agent status: online, working, idle or blocked
@mentions and chat with agents inside task threads
Deliverable review, with a lead agent that checks work before it ships
Live activity feed and analytics across all agents
Recurring tasks (Pro and up) and Cloud VM provisioning (Scale)

pricing.note: Yearly billing saves about 17% ($140, $290 and $790 a year). An AI provider subscription or API key is required on top.

dart.meta: Dart is an AI project management tool where teams and AI agents share tasks, docs and roadmaps. Free for up to 4 teammates; paid from $8/user/mo.
long: Dart is a project management workspace where people and AI agents work side by side. AI agents can be assigned tasks and execute them, and Dart's AI also plans roadmaps, generates subtasks, fills task properties and writes reports.
It suits startups and teams that want a Linear- or Asana-style tracker with AI built in, and it connects to ChatGPT, Claude and any LLM through its MCP server.
features: AI agents that take assigned tasks and do the work
AI subtask generation, property filling, reporting and duplicate detection
List, board, roadmap and calendar layouts with sprints and time tracking
MCP server plus ChatGPT and Claude integrations
Slack, Discord, GitHub, Notion, Zapier and n8n integrations
Desktop apps for Mac, Windows and Linux, plus iOS and Android apps

tiers: up to 4 teammates, AI agents included
unlimited teammates, AI chat and roadmap planning, GitHub and Slack
SAML SSO and SCIM, analytics, priority support
pricing.note: Paid prices shown are with yearly billing (20% off).

ai-emaily.meta: AI Emaily is an AI email client whose agent triages, drafts in your voice and schedules across every provider. Paid plans from $14.99/mo, 7-day trial.
long: AI Emaily is an AI-native email client with an autonomous assistant that triages your inbox, drafts replies in your voice, schedules meetings and closes loops. It unifies Gmail, Outlook and other providers in one inbox on every device.
It is built for busy professionals and teams who want an agent to handle email work while they stay in control, with undo and an audit trail on actions.
features: Works with every major email provider in one unified inbox
Inbox triage and voice-matched reply drafting
Scheduling and follow-ups handled by the assistant
Autopilot mode that can act on email on its own
Filters cold pitches and noise into a digest
BYOK, multi-model and MCP tools on Autopilot and Team plans

tiers: listed in the maker's site summary
1,000 AI credits a month, up to 5 accounts
pricing.note: Annual billing lowers these to about $12.42, $20.75 and $14.92 a month.

context-dev.meta: Context.dev is a web data API for AI agents: scrape pages to Markdown, search the web, crawl sites, extract JSON. Free 1,000 credits; paid from $19/mo.
long: Context.dev is a web data API for AI agents and AI apps. One API key lets you scrape any page into clean Markdown, search the live web and news, crawl whole sites, extract structured JSON against your own schema and monitor pages for changes.
It is for developers building agents, RAG pipelines and products that need fresh web context, with SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go and PHP.
features: Scrape any page to Markdown, with JS rendering and proxies included
Crawl up to 500 pages per call, plus Map for URL discovery
Web and news search APIs and an Answers endpoint
Structured JSON extraction against your schema
Page monitors and batch jobs with webhooks
Brand, logo and styleguide data APIs

pricing.note: Annual billing gives two months free. One standard scrape costs 1 credit.

betterclaw.meta: BetterClaw is a no-code AI agent builder: deploy agents to Slack, Telegram, Discord or Gmail on 28+ model providers. Free plan; paid from $19/mo.
long: BetterClaw lets you build and deploy AI agents without code or servers. You create an agent, pick a model, connect channels and tools, and it runs recurring jobs on a schedule in Slack, Telegram, Discord or Gmail.
It is aimed at non-technical users, solo operators and agencies who want an always-on agent without self-hosting OpenClaw. Every plan is bring-your-own-key, with no markup on model costs.
features: No-code agent setup, with most agents deployed in under a minute
Models from 28+ providers, bring your own key with zero markup
Connectors for Slack, Telegram, Discord, Gmail and more
Docker-isolated sandbox, kill switch and AES-256 encrypted credentials
Health monitoring that auto-pauses misbehaving agents
Team seats with role-based access on Pro and Business

pricing.note: Annual billing drops Pro to $39/mo and Business to $119/mo. Model API usage is paid to your provider.

clawdi.meta: Clawdi hosts always-on Hermes or OpenClaw AI agents in the cloud, with shared memory, skills and connectors. Cloud Agent plans $10 or $20 a month.
long: Clawdi is a home for AI agents with shared context. It runs always-on Hermes or OpenClaw agents in the cloud without a server to maintain, and you chat with them over Telegram, Discord or WhatsApp.
A free, MIT-licensed CLI also connects agents on your own computer, such as Claude Code and Codex, so memories, skills, vaults and connectors are shared across every agent.
features: Deploy a cloud Hermes or OpenClaw agent in minutes
Chat through Telegram, Discord or WhatsApp
Shared memories, skills and secret vaults across agents
Gmail, Notion, GitHub and hundreds more connectors via one-click OAuth
Free MIT-licensed CLI to connect Claude Code, Codex and other local agents
Clawdi AI pay-as-you-go models, or bring your own key

pricing.note: The open-source stack can also be self-hosted.

momen.meta: Momen is a no-code full-stack AI app builder with a real database, logic, AI agents and publishing. Free plan; paid from $33 per project/mo.
long: Momen is a no-code full-stack app builder. You visually build the frontend, database, backend logic (Actionflows), APIs and AI agents, then publish to your own domain.
It is for founders and makers who want a production app with real data and payments without writing code, and it supports bringing your own AI model on paid plans.
features: Visual builder for frontend, database and backend logic
Built-in AI agents with bring-your-own-model on paid plans
Automated Actionflows on schedules and database triggers
APIs, payments, SSO and custom domains
Usage-based add-ons for storage, data transfer and AI points
Dedicated instance and BYOC deployment options

tiers: publishing, custom domain, unlimited AI agents
pricing.note: Prices shown are with annual billing (save up to 15%). Extra resources are billed as add-ons.

scalebrowser.meta: Scalebrowser gives each AI agent its own persistent browser that stays signed in and handles captchas, via MCP, SDK or CDP. From $19/mo, 7-day trial.
long: Scalebrowser is a browser app built for AI agents. Each agent gets its own isolated profile with a persistent identity, so it stays signed in across runs with stored logins, passkeys and cookies, and it handles captchas and email confirmation codes.
It is for automation builders running many accounts or identities. Agents connect over MCP, Python and Node SDKs or direct CDP, so existing browser-use or Playwright-style agents can switch over.
features: Unlimited profiles, each with a persistent identity
Stored logins, passkeys and cookies that stay on your machine
Captcha handling and an inbox for email confirmation codes
MCP, Python and Node SDKs, REST API and direct CDP
Human takeover plus detailed trails with screenshots
Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor and custom agents

pricing.note: All plans include unlimited profiles. Fleet extends at +5 browsers for $40/mo or +1 machine for $25/mo.

cochat.meta: CoChat is an AI research workspace whose agents gather verified sources, compare models and automate work. Free plan; paid $9 or $19 a month.
long: CoChat is an AI research workspace that verifies every source. Its agents gather citations, check them and organize findings, with side-by-side model comparison and real-time collaboration.
It suits researchers, students and teams. CoChat connects to 80+ tools and can run automations, with approval gates before risky actions.
features: Citation verification for research sources
Side-by-side model comparison
Real-time team collaboration
Zotero storage and file uploads
Automations across 80+ integrations, with approval gates
Cloud workspace to run code (Pro)

tiers: 10x Starter usage, unlimited verifications and automations
pricing.note: No credit card needed to start.

coddo.meta: Coddo is a Mac app that adds a visual interface, Kanban boards and voice dictation to Claude Code and Codex. Free to start; Basic $7/mo.
long: Coddo Desktop turns terminal AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex into a visual app, with chat, Kanban boards, Git integration and multi-project support. It ships with Whisper Island, a voice dictation tool that works anywhere on your Mac.
It is for developers who use CLI coding agents but want a visual workflow and voice input. Coddo is made in France.
features: Visual chat interface for Claude Code and Codex
Unlimited Kanban boards for agent tasks
Full Git integration and multi-project support
Custom skills
Whisper Island voice dictation anywhere on macOS

long: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent. It runs in your terminal and is also available as a desktop app (in beta), and it works with many model providers rather than a single vendor.

It ships with two built-in agents you switch between with the Tab key: build, the default full-access agent for development work, and plan, a read-only agent for analysis and code exploration that asks permission before running bash commands. A general subagent handles complex searches and multistep tasks.
opencode.who: Developers who want an open-source terminal coding agent they can point at the model provider of their choice, including people exploring unfamiliar codebases with the read-only plan agent.
features: Terminal coding agent plus a desktop app (beta)
Works with many model providers
Built-in build (full access) and plan (read-only) agents, switched with Tab
General subagent for complex searches and multistep tasks

long: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal. It understands your codebase and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code and handling git workflows through natural language commands.
You can use it in the terminal, in your IDE, or by tagging @claude on GitHub. Anthropic notes that installing it via npm is deprecated in favor of its recommended install methods.
claude-code.who: Developers who want an AI agent that works directly in their terminal and repository, and teams already on a Claude plan or the Anthropic API.
features: Runs in the terminal and reads your codebase
Executes routine tasks and explains complex code
Handles git workflows with natural language
Works in IDEs and via @claude on GitHub

long: Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer. It is open source and can be used with a ChatGPT plan or the OpenAI API.

Beyond the terminal, Codex can be installed in code editors such as VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf, has a desktop app experience (codex app), and has a cloud-based agent, Codex Web, at chatgpt.com/codex. Standalone installers are available for macOS, Linux and Windows.
openai-codex-cli.who: Developers who want OpenAI's open-source coding agent in their terminal or editor, especially those who already have a ChatGPT plan.
features: Local coding agent that runs on your computer
Editor extensions for VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf
Desktop app and a cloud agent (Codex Web)
Installers for macOS, Linux and Windows

long: Graphify turns a project into a knowledge graph that coding assistants can query instead of grepping through files. You type /graphify in your AI coding assistant and it maps your code, docs, PDFs, images and videos.

Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter, deterministically and without an LLM, so nothing leaves your machine; docs, PDFs and media use your assistant's model or a configured API key. Every edge is tagged as extracted from the source or inferred, and it is a real graph rather than a vector index. A separate hosted product, Graphify Cloud, adds always-on, cross-repo features with a free 14-day trial.
graphify.who: Developers using AI coding assistants on larger projects who want the agent to navigate code and docs through a structured map rather than raw file search.
features: /graphify command inside your coding assistant
Local tree-sitter code parsing with no LLM
Edges labeled EXTRACTED or INFERRED
Graph you can traverse, not an embedding index
Optional hosted Graphify Cloud

long: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source AI agent that brings Gemini into your terminal, giving lightweight, direct access from your prompt to the model.

Its README notes that for unpaid-tier and Google One users, Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026, and that Gemini CLI is not optimized for the latest Gemini models; Google points to Antigravity for the best coding experience with them.
gemini-cli.who: Developers who want an open-source terminal agent for Gemini models. Check the current README first, since Google now recommends Antigravity CLI for many users.
features: Open-source terminal agent for Gemini
Lightweight, direct prompt-to-model access
Successor for unpaid tier: Antigravity CLI (per the README)

long: Claude-Mem is a persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code. It preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool-usage observations, generating semantic summaries and making them available to future sessions.

That lets the agent keep continuity of knowledge about a project after sessions end or reconnect. The installer offers a hosted memory option with a 30-day free trial after a sign-in, and a local observer is available as an opt-in.
claude-mem.who: Claude Code users (and other coding-agent users) who are tired of re-explaining a project at the start of every session.
features: Captures tool-usage observations automatically
Generates semantic summaries for later sessions
Keeps project knowledge across sessions and reconnects
Hosted memory with a free trial, or an opt-in local observer

long: Orca is an agent development environment for running coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or Pi side by side, each in its own git worktree and tracked in one place.

You can fan one prompt across several agents, compare the results and merge the winner, review diffs and send line comments back to an agent, browse PRs and issues in-app, and run agents on a remote machine. A mobile companion app lets you monitor agents and send follow-ups from your phone.
orca.who: Developers who run several coding agents in parallel on their own subscriptions and want one place to launch, compare and review their work.
features: Parallel agents in isolated git worktrees
Fan out one prompt and merge the best result
Diff review with comments sent back to the agent
Remote machines with auto-reconnect and port forwarding
Mobile companion app

long: OpenHands is an open-source platform for autonomous coding agents. Its Agent Canvas is a self-hosted developer control center for starting agent conversations and automating everyday tasks, such as publishing reports to Slack or breaking GitHub issues down into tasks.

It runs locally by default but can connect to local, remote and cloud backends, and it can run OpenHands as well as other agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode or any ACP-compatible agent. A paid cloud option is also offered.
openhands.who: Engineering teams and developers who want a self-hosted, always-on setup for coding agents and automations, with the option of a hosted cloud.
features: Self-hosted Agent Canvas control center
Runs OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other ACP agents
Local, remote and cloud backends
Automations such as Slack reports and GitHub issue breakdowns

long: Cline is an open-source coding agent that works in your IDE, in the terminal and as a desktop app. In VS Code it creates files, runs commands, browses the web and uses tools, with human-in-the-loop approval for each step.

There is also a CLI for interactive chat or fully headless runs in CI/CD and scripts, a native desktop app for macOS and Windows that can schedule routines and manage models, plugins and MCP servers, and a JetBrains plugin.
cline.who: Developers who want an open-source coding agent inside VS Code or JetBrains with step-by-step approvals, plus teams that want to script it in CI.
features: VS Code extension with human-in-the-loop approvals
CLI with headless mode for CI/CD
Desktop app for macOS and Windows
JetBrains plugin
MCP server management

long: Strix is an open-source AI penetration-testing tool: autonomous agents that act like real attackers, run your code dynamically, find vulnerabilities and validate them with actual proofs of concept.
It integrates with GitHub Actions and CI/CD pipelines so it can scan every pull request and block insecure code before it reaches production. A cloud offering sits alongside the open-source project.
strix.who: Developers and security teams who want fast, automated security testing of their own applications, including in CI.
features: Autonomous pentesting agents
Findings validated with proofs of concept
GitHub Actions and CI/CD integration
Open source with a cloud option

long: Open Interpreter is a coding agent optimized for low-cost models. It is a fork of OpenAI's Codex that focuses on emulating the agent harness that gets the best performance out of cheaper and open-weight models.

A /harness command switches the active harness, it works in ACP-compatible editors via interpreter acp, and it speaks the same Codex exec protocol, so Codex SDK users can switch with a one-line change. You start a session by typing i or interpreter in your terminal.
open-interpreter.who: Developers who want a terminal coding agent that gets more out of low-cost or open-weight models than general-purpose harnesses do.
features: Fork of OpenAI's Codex tuned for low-cost models
Switchable harness modes via /harness
Works in ACP-compatible editors
Compatible with the Codex SDK exec protocol

long: goose is a general-purpose, open-source AI agent that runs on your machine. It is not just for code: it can also be used for research, writing, automation and data analysis.

It comes as a native desktop app for macOS, Linux and Windows, a full CLI and an API, and is built in Rust. goose works with 15+ providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure and Bedrock, using API keys or existing Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini subscriptions via ACP, and connects to extensions through MCP.
goose.who: Developers and power users who want one local agent, with a desktop app or CLI, that can install, run, edit and test code with the model of their choice.
features: Desktop app, CLI and API
Built in Rust
15+ model providers, including local models via Ollama
Uses existing Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini subscriptions via ACP
MCP extensions

long: Herdr is a runtime for running and managing many coding agents side by side. It owns their terminals rather than wrapping or replacing the agents, so it works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok and others.

Terminals keep running in a background server when you close the client or lose an SSH connection, and after a restart herdr restores the saved layout and can resume supported sessions. It combines local and SSH machines in one window, marks every pane as working, blocked or idle, and lets agents drive it through a CLI and socket API.
herdr.who: Developers juggling several terminal coding agents across one or more machines who want to see at a glance which one needs attention.
features: Background server keeps sessions alive
Local and SSH machines in one window
Pane status: working, blocked or idle
CLI and socket API for agents
tmux-style keys plus mouse; plugins

long: Codewhale is an open-source coding agent that works with any model. It reads your project, edits files, runs commands and checks its own work in your terminal, using a hosted or local model you choose.
It is written in Rust, with tool approvals and review flows, and its installer downloads checksum-verified binaries for macOS and Linux.
codewhale.who: Developers who want a model-agnostic terminal coding agent, including people running local models.
features: Works with hosted or local models
Reads, edits and runs commands in your project
Tool approvals and review flows
Rust engine with checksum-verified installers

long: Oh My Claudecode (OMC) is a multi-agent orchestration layer for Claude Code. It coordinates teams of specialized agents so you can use Claude Code's power without learning all of its configuration, under the tagline "zero learning curve."
It installs through the Claude Code plugin marketplace (recommended) or an npm CLI, and the same maintainers offer oh-my-codex for OpenAI Codex CLI users.
oh-my-claudecode.who: Claude Code users who want ready-made multi-agent workflows rather than building their own agent teams.
features: Multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code
Install via the Claude Code marketplace or npm
Sister project oh-my-codex for Codex CLI

long: DeepSeek-Reasonix is an open-source (MIT) coding agent for your terminal, desktop, browser and editor, built for complex software-engineering tasks on DeepSeek models. It runs on your computer with the model of your choice.

It reads your project, edits files and runs commands and tests. You can have it ask before each step or work on its own within limits you set, and files its edit tools changed can be rewound. A Studio desktop app is the suggested starting point.
deepseek-reasonix.who: Developers who want an open-source coding agent tuned for DeepSeek models, with approval controls and the ability to undo edits.
features: Terminal, desktop, browser and editor clients
Ask-before-each-step or autonomous within limits
Rewind files changed by its edit tools
MIT license; model of your choice

long: Oh My Pi is a terminal coding agent with IDE features wired in, built by Stencil Labs as a fork of Pi by Mario Zechner.
Its README lists 60+ providers, 31 built-in tools, 14 LSP operations and 28 debugger (DAP) operations on a Rust core of about 80k lines.
oh-my-pi.who: Developers who want a terminal coding agent with language-server and debugger capabilities built in, and support for many model providers.
features: 60+ model providers
31 built-in tools
LSP and DAP (debugger) operations
Rust core; fork of Pi

long: PentAGI is an open-source, self-hosted multi-agent system for autonomous penetration testing. You describe a target and a goal in plain language, and a team of specialized AI agents plans the work, runs 20+ professional tools such as nmap, Metasploit and sqlmap inside an isolated Docker sandbox, and hands you a report.

It runs on your own servers with your choice of model: 10+ cloud LLM providers, your own OpenAI-compatible gateway, or local models through Ollama or vLLM. Results are kept in PostgreSQL with pgvector, and an optional Neo4j knowledge graph tracks hosts, services and findings.
pentagi.who: Security engineers, penetration testers, researchers and red teams who want an autonomous assistant on their own infrastructure, for authorized testing only.
features: Plain-language targets and goals
20+ security tools in an isolated Docker sandbox
10+ cloud LLM providers or local models
Memory in PostgreSQL/pgvector; optional Neo4j graph
Generated reports

long: Context Mode is an MCP server that optimizes a coding agent's context window. Its README describes how raw tool output, such as a Playwright snapshot (56 KB) or twenty GitHub issues (59 KB), quickly fills the context.

Sandboxed tools keep raw data out of the context (the README cites 315 KB reduced to 5.4 KB), and every file edit, git operation, task, error and decision is tracked in SQLite and retrieved by search after the conversation compacts, so the agent picks up where it left off.
context-mode.who: Heavy users of coding agents and MCP tools who keep running out of context or losing track of work after compaction.
features: MCP server that sandboxes tool output
Session events tracked in SQLite
BM25 search retrieves only relevant context after compaction
Large context savings reported by the maker

long: AgentMemory is a persistent memory layer for AI coding agents, so your agent remembers your project instead of needing it re-explained. It supports Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Hermes, OpenClaw, pi, OpenCode and any MCP client.

It builds on Andrej Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern with confidence scoring, lifecycle, knowledge graphs and hybrid search. It needs Node.js 20 or newer, and the first run is an interactive setup where you pick which agents to wire up and an LLM provider, or stay keyless.
agentmemory.who: Developers who use one or more coding agents and want memory that carries across sessions and tools.
features: Works with many coding agents and any MCP client
Confidence scoring, lifecycle and knowledge graphs
Hybrid search
Interactive setup; keyless option

long: Crush is Charm's terminal coding agent, described as "your new coding bestie" for your favorite terminal. It wires your tools, code and workflows into the LLM of your choice.

You can choose from many LLMs or add your own via OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible APIs, switch models mid-session while keeping context, keep multiple sessions per project, use LSPs for extra context and add capabilities through MCP (http, stdio and sse).
crush.who: Developers who live in the terminal and want a polished TUI coding agent that is not tied to one model.
features: Multi-model, including OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible APIs
Switch models mid-session
Multiple sessions per project
LSP-enhanced context
MCP support (http, stdio, sse)

long: Qwen Code is the Qwen team's open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser and chat.

It includes auto-memory, auto-skills, subagents, agent teams and MCP out of the box. The framework and the Qwen models are open source, and it supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs as well as third-party providers and local models via Ollama or vLLM, switchable at runtime. IDE plugins, a desktop app, a web UI and SDKs are available.
qwen-code.who: Developers who want an open-source coding agent that pairs naturally with open Qwen models but can switch to other providers or local models.
features: Auto-memory, auto-skills, subagents and agent teams
MCP support
OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen and local models
IDE plugins, desktop app, web UI and SDKs

long: Vibe Kanban is a kanban board for planning and running tasks with coding agents such as Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex and Amp. You plan work as kanban issues, privately or with a team, then create workspaces where agents execute them.
Note: the project's README says Vibe Kanban is sunsetting, so check the announcement before adopting it.
vibe-kanban.who: Developers and teams who spend much of their time planning and reviewing coding-agent work. Because the project is sunsetting, it suits existing users more than new adopters.
features: Plan with kanban issues
Run coding agents in workspaces
Works with Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex and Amp
Project is sunsetting (per README)

long: Beads (bd) is a distributed, graph-based issue tracker for AI agents, powered by Dolt. It gives coding agents persistent, structured memory by replacing messy Markdown plans with a dependency-aware graph.

That lets agents handle long-horizon tasks without losing context. It is a CLI you install once and use everywhere, and bd init sets up AGENTS.md so agents can discover the workflow, with project setup for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. It runs on macOS, Linux, Windows and FreeBSD.
beads.who: Developers who give coding agents long-running, multi-step work and want the plan stored as a structured graph rather than ad hoc notes.
features: Dependency-aware issue graph for agents
Powered by Dolt
bd init writes AGENTS.md
Claude Code, Codex and Cursor setup
macOS, Linux, Windows, FreeBSD

long: Planning With Files is a planning skill for AI coding agents that keeps the plan on disk. It maintains task_plan.md, findings.md and progress.md files, so the plan survives context loss, /clear, crashes and compaction.
Rather than a prompt the agent might ignore, it uses lifecycle hooks that fire every turn to inject the relevant planning context. Recovery reads project files only.
planning-with-files.who: Coding-agent users working on long tasks who lose the thread when context is cleared or compacted.
features: Persistent Markdown plan files
Lifecycle hooks inject the plan every turn
Survives /clear, crashes and compaction

long: Happy Coder is an open-source (MIT) mobile and desktop app for running and controlling coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex with the subscriptions you already pay for. It adds a harness, not another bill.

It runs on your own hardware and your projects stay ordinary folders. Sessions are available on your phone with end-to-end encryption between devices, and it is multiplayer: you can invite someone into a session so you both watch and steer the same agent.
happy-coder.who: People who use Claude Code, Codex or similar agents and want to monitor and steer them from their phone or share sessions with a colleague.
features: Uses your existing Claude, Codex and other subscriptions
End-to-end encrypted mobile app
Multiplayer sessions
Runs on your own hardware; MIT license

long: Paseo is an open-source agentic development environment for desktop, mobile, web and CLI, with one interface for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode, Pi and other agents.

The desktop app puts agents, editor, terminals, diffs, pull requests and a browser in one window. You can run many agents at once, each in its own worktree, on one or several machines; agents can create worktrees and launch and talk to other agents. The native iOS and Android app is the full app.
paseo.who: Developers who orchestrate several coding agents and want the same environment on desktop and phone, running on their own machines.
features: Parallel agents in separate worktrees
Agents can launch and message other agents
Editor, terminals, diffs, PRs and browser in one window
Self-hosted; native iOS and Android apps

long: jcode is a high-performance coding agent harness written in Rust, designed to run dozens of agents in parallel with low memory use and no lag. Its README publishes memory and latency benchmarks against other agents.

When you spawn two or more agents in the same repo, its server manages them for native collaboration: if one agent edits a file another has read, the second is notified and can check the diff for conflicts.
jcode.who: Developers who fan out many coding agents at once and care about resource use and agent-to-agent coordination.
features: Rust harness built for many parallel agents
Headless swarm workers
Server notifies agents of conflicting edits
SDK and published benchmarks

long: Coder is a self-hosted platform for cloud development environments and AI coding agents. Workspaces are defined in Terraform (EC2 VMs, Kubernetes pods, Docker containers and more), connected through a secure WireGuard tunnel, and automatically shut down when idle.

Coder Agents runs a native AI coding agent whose loop executes in the control plane on your infrastructure, with no API keys in workspaces. It supports any model (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock or self-hosted) with centralized model governance, cost tracking and audit logging.
coder.who: Platform and engineering teams that want governed, self-hosted dev environments for both developers and AI agents.
features: Terraform-defined workspaces
Auto-shutdown of idle resources
Coding agents running on your infrastructure
Bring any model; no LLM keys in workspaces
Governance, cost tracking and audit logs

long: DeepCode is an open agentic coding system from HKUDS that uses multi-agent orchestration to turn research papers and natural-language specs into code.
It provides TUI, desktop and web clients over one shared local service, which share projects, session history, models, skills, permissions, goals and automations.
deepcode.who: Researchers and developers who want to turn papers or written specifications into working code with a multi-agent system.
features: Paper- and spec-to-code generation
Multi-agent orchestration
TUI, desktop and web clients over one local service

long: Superset is an agentic IDE for running Claude Code, Codex or another CLI agent with terminals, code review and browser previews in one workspace, so you can orchestrate many agents in parallel.

You add a repository, create a workspace, choose a CLI agent and describe a change, then inspect the patch, run tests and preview your app in the browser pane before committing. It targets macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), with an experimental Linux AppImage; Git is the only requirement.
superset.who: Developers on macOS who run CLI coding agents and want review and preview built into the same workspace.
features: Works with Claude Code, Codex and other CLI agents
Parallel workspaces
Change review, terminals and browser preview
macOS app; experimental Linux build

long: MiMo Code is Xiaomi's terminal-native AI coding assistant. It reads and writes code, runs commands, manages Git and uses a persistent memory system to keep an understanding of your project across sessions.

It works with major model providers and is tuned for Xiaomi's MiMo models. It is also the core engine of the Xiaomi MiMo Desktop app, which handles office work, design, coding and multimodal creation.
mimo-code.who: Developers who want a terminal coding agent with long-term project memory, especially those using Xiaomi's MiMo models.
features: Reads and writes code, runs commands and manages Git
Persistent project memory across sessions
Smart orchestration across models and tools
Powers the MiMo Desktop app

long: Qodo makes AI code review and testing agents that work in the IDE, the terminal and pull requests to catch issues before merge. It integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, and offers a free version for open-source projects.
Its open-source PR-Agent project, now community-maintained and described as a legacy project of Qodo, is separate from Qodo's main code-review product.
qodo.who: Development teams that want automated, AI-assisted code review on pull requests across common Git hosts.
features: AI code review on pull requests
IDE and terminal agents
GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps
Free version for open-source projects

long: Agent Orchestrator (Orchestrator.inc) runs and supervises teams of coding agents from planning to merge. It is a local desktop workspace where each coding task gets its own agent, workspace and feedback loop.

For Git-backed work each worker gets its own branch and worktree, and a project-aware orchestrator plans and delegates larger outcomes. A live kanban follows every worker, pull request, CI run and review.
agent-orchestrator.who: Developers running several coding agents across one project who need help splitting work, avoiding branch collisions and following changes through review.
features: Per-task agent, workspace and branch/worktree
Project-aware orchestrator for larger goals
Live kanban of workers, PRs, CI and reviews
Choice of coding agent and model per task

long: HumanLayer is a multiplayer coding-agent IDE and cloud that brings agent sessions, plan artifacts and code diffs together so a team can collaborate and ship.

You bring your own AI subscriptions or API keys, such as Claude or Codex, so there is no separate per-token bill. The company says it is SOC 2 Type II compliant, with ZDR and DPA agreements on enterprise tiers. Its older open-source code on GitHub is marked deprecated in favor of the rebuild at humanlayer.com.
humanlayer.who: Engineering teams who want to collaborate with each other and with coding agents on plans and diffs in one shared place.
features: Real-time human and agent collaboration on artifacts
Bring your own subscriptions or keys
Remote daemons
SOC 2 Type II (per the maker)

long: OpenChamber is an open-source workspace for running and reviewing AI coding work on desktop, web, VS Code and mobile, built around the OpenCode agent. Your projects and sessions stay available when you switch devices.

Session Goals keep an agent working until it reaches a goal, gets blocked or hits a limit you set. Multi-run sends one task to up to five models so you can compare results or merge the best parts with Fusion, and Changes Walkthrough turns a large diff into a guided tour.
openchamber.who: OpenCode users who want a richer interface to run, compare and review agent work across devices.
features: Desktop, web, VS Code and mobile
Session Goals
Multi-run across up to five models, plus Fusion
Changes Walkthrough for large diffs

long: Open SWE is LangChain's open-source asynchronous coding agent, built on Deep Agents. It investigates a codebase, implements changes, validates them and delivers a pull request, and it can review PRs, monitor CI and respond to feedback.

Its README says it is under active development with breaking changes, is not accepting issues or contributions, and that deploying it as is requires access to the Managed Deep Agents private beta; otherwise LangChain suggests forking and adapting it.
open-swe.who: Teams experimenting with background coding agents that take work from issues and return pull requests, and who are comfortable adapting early-stage code.
features: Issue-to-pull-request workflow
PR reviews that learn repo preferences
CI monitoring and feedback responses
Built on LangChain Deep Agents

long: Trail Code is a self-learning context layer for coding agents. It gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others a map of your code, plus what your team has learned about it, to make them faster and cheaper on large codebases.
The maker reports 46% fewer tool calls and 60% less time, and publishes SWE-bench Verified and cost comparisons. It was previously called Graft, and graft commands still work.
trail-code.who: Teams using coding agents on large codebases who want to cut tool calls, tokens and time.
features: Code map for coding agents
Team learnings shared with agents
Works with Claude Code, Cursor and Codex
Published benchmark results

long: Ralph for Claude Code is an autonomous development loop that keeps Claude Code iterating on your project until a task is complete. It implements Geoffrey Huntley's "Ralph" technique.

Safeguards prevent infinite loops and API overuse: a dual-condition exit gate needs both completion indicators and an explicit exit signal, there is configurable rate limiting (100 calls an hour by default) and a circuit breaker with error detection. It installs once as a global command.
ralph-for-claude-code.who: Claude Code users who want hands-off, iterative development runs with guardrails.
features: Continuous autonomous loops for Claude Code
Dual-condition exit detection
Configurable rate limiting
Circuit breaker for runaway loops

long: Hunk is an interactive terminal diff viewer for reviewing code changes, including what coding agents changed. It is built on OpenTUI and Pierre diffs.

It offers a multi-file review stream with sidebar navigation, inline AI and agent annotations beside the code, split and unified layouts, a watch mode and Git difftool support. Prebuilt binaries cover macOS, Linux and Windows x64.
hunk.who: Developers who review agent-generated changes in the terminal and want a faster, review-first diff view.
features: Multi-file review stream
Inline agent annotations
Split, unified and auto layouts
Watch mode and Git difftool support

long: Oh My OpenCode Slim is an agent orchestration plugin for OpenCode. It includes a built-in team of specialized agents that can scout a codebase, look up fresh documentation, review architecture, handle UI work and carry out well-scoped implementation tasks.

An orchestrator plans the work, dispatches specialists as background tasks and reconciles their results, routing each part of the job to the best-suited agent to balance quality, speed and cost. You can mix any models.
oh-my-opencode-slim.who: OpenCode users who want a lean, ready-made multi-agent setup with automatic task delegation.
features: Six specialized agents under one orchestrator
Automatic delegation as background tasks
Mix any models

long: Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp and Pi.

It plugs into your agent through hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a plan or HTML, or finishes writing code, the work opens in your browser so you can mark it up, comment on diffs or PRs, suggest code and send the feedback straight back to the agent.
plannotator.who: Developers who want to review and annotate agent plans and diffs visually before the agent continues.
features: Annotate plans, specs, Markdown and HTML
Review local diffs and remote PRs
Feedback goes straight back to the agent
Works with many coding agents

long: Terax is a lightweight, open-source, terminal-first AI development environment built on Tauri 2, Rust and React 19. It is about 7-8 MB on disk, with no telemetry and no account.

It combines a native PTY terminal with WebGL rendering, an agentic AI side panel that uses your own keys or fully local models, a code editor, file explorer, source control with a git graph and a web preview pane. Its maker says it is returning to active development, with a major v0.9.0 update in progress.
terax.who: Developers who want a small, private, terminal-centered workspace with an AI agent built in.
features: Native terminal with WebGL rendering
AI side panel with your own keys or local models
Editor, file explorer and git graph
No telemetry, no account

long: Worktrunk is a CLI for Git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel. Git worktrees give each agent its own working directory so agents don't step on each other.

Three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches, and there are quality-of-life features such as hooks to automate local workflows and copy-on-write build caches. Full documentation is at worktrunk.dev.
worktrunk.who: Developers running several coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex at once on the same repository.
features: Simple worktree commands
Hooks for local workflows
Copy-on-write build caches

long: Munder Difflin is a free, open-source multi-agent harness that runs terminal coding agents together like an office, using the subscriptions you already pay for.

It wraps Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok, Kimi Code, Qwen, OpenCode, Crush, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor and more, with bring-your-own keys and local LLMs. Agents message, route and remember, coordinated by a lead agent and shown as avatars on a shared office floor. Downloads are available for macOS, Windows and Linux.
munder-difflin.who: Developers who want to coordinate many terminal coding agents on their own machine with a visual overview.
features: Wraps many terminal coding agents
Uses existing subscriptions, your own keys or local LLMs
Agent messaging, routing and memory
Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux

long: mini-SWE-agent is a tiny coding agent from the SWE-bench and SWE-agent team, with about 100 lines of Python for the agent class. It solves GitHub issues or helps on the command line.

The team reports it scores above 74% on SWE-bench Verified and starts faster than Claude Code. It supports local environments, Docker or Podman, Singularity/Apptainer and more, and the README says it is used by Meta, NVIDIA, IBM, Princeton and Stanford, among others.
mini-swe-agent.who: Researchers and developers who want a minimal, hackable agent for benchmarks, evaluations or simple command-line help.

long: SuperPlane is an open-source factory for one-shot engineering. It turns high-confidence backlog issues into verified, review-ready pull requests so engineers can focus on work that needs judgment.

It coordinates coding agents, source control, CI, review, approvals and feedback in one visible system, evaluates which issues agents can handle with confidence, applies the same guardrails to every run and sends failures back to the agent with context. It is built on an Apache 2.0 engine and can run in the cloud or on-prem.
superplane.who: Engineering teams that want to automate routine backlog work with agents while keeping ambiguous decisions with people.

Workflow-level guardrails on every run
Coordinates agents, CI, review and approvals
Apache 2.0 engine; cloud or on-prem

long: Gentle AI configures the coding agents you already use with shared rules, skills and settings, describing itself as a deterministic engineering environment that gives your agent memory, a workflow and evidence.
Its Engram component lets the agent write down what it learns and consult it before asking you, so context builds up across sessions. The README lists 17 integrations with native configuration.
gentle-ai.who: Developers who want consistent rules, memory and workflow across the coding agents they already use.
features: Shared rules, skills and settings for existing agents
Engram memory across sessions
17 integrations

long: OpenRig builds persistent teams of coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pi. You define your agent team in YAML and boot it with one command, and the agents are managed as one system.

You talk to a lead agent about the outcome you want, and it coordinates specialists and brings back results and decisions that need your attention, keeping the team's work and context in stable places.
openrig.who: Developers who want to run Claude Code, Codex and other agents as an organized, long-lived team rather than separate terminal sessions.
features: Agent teams defined in YAML
Claude Code and Codex in the same rig
Lead agent coordinates specialists

long: Backlog.md is a Markdown-native task manager and kanban visualizer for any Git repository. It turns a folder into a self-contained project board powered by plain Markdown files and a zero-config CLI.

It structures agent work around review checkpoints: the agent first breaks your idea into tasks with descriptions, acceptance criteria and milestones, so you can review the specs before any code exists.
backlog-md.who: Developers who coordinate work between people and AI agents and want task specs reviewed before code is written.

Tasks with acceptance criteria and milestones
Review checkpoints for agent work
